Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

compromise noun and verb

also make a compromise, reach a compromise, meet halfway, give and take, concession

classical

Cic. Rab. Post. 31 (Lewis & Short)

aliquid dē suō remittere

give up something of one’s own: compromise

Latin has no noun for a compromise; it says what each side does. When both give way, uterque aliquid dē suō remittit; the terms agreed are a condiciō or pactum (see agreement).

Other words

  • dē suō jūre dēcēdere — give up part of one’s rights, yield a point

    also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 27; Att. 16.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • comprōmissum, comprōmissī n. — an agreement to go to arbitration

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · Cic. Rosc. Com. 12 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A false friend: the parties’ promise to abide by an arbiter’s award, a legal term, not a compromise.

Examples

  • Uterque aliquid dē suō remittat.

    Let each of you give up something.composed

See also agreement, agree, agree.

SourcesLewis & Short: remitto · Lewis & Short: decedo · Lewis & Short: compromissum
